name: Th1 cell
summary: A helper T cell that directs the defence against microbes living inside cells, such as viruses and Mycobacteria. Steered by IL-12 from dendritic cells, it makes IFN-γ, which makes macrophages kill the microbes they have swallowed, and it helps CD8 T cells. It is the helper arm of cell-mediated immunity.
functions: Develops in the lymph node from a naive CD4 T cell activated by a dendritic cell. IL-12 from dendritic cells and macrophages, and IFN-γ from NK cells and T cells, switch on the transcription factor T-bet, which fixes the Th1 programme.
Makes IFN-γ as its signature cytokine, together with TNF and IL-2.

Activates macrophages: IFN-γ and CD40L on contact switch on their killing machinery, so they can destroy microbes that survive inside them, such as Mycobacteria. People with inherited defects in the IL-12 and IFN-γ pathway are very susceptible to these microbes.
Helps CD8 T cells, partly directly through IL-2 and mostly indirectly by licensing the dendritic cell with CD40L, which improves CD8 T-cell responses and memory.
Restrains competing helper cells: IFN-γ blocks naive CD4 T cells from becoming Th2 or Th17 cells (shown mainly in mouse experiments).
Leaves the lymph node in the efferent lymph, enters the blood and is drawn to infected tissue by CXCL9 and CXCL10 acting on CXCR3, where macrophages and dendritic cells present antigen to it again.
Debated: how stable the Th1 state is. Th1 cells can take on features of other helper subsets, and many researchers now see helper subsets as flexible states rather than fixed lineages.
Was first defined in mouse T-cell clones, and mouse strains differ: C57BL/6 mice tend toward Th1 responses, BALB/c mice toward Th2. Human cells show the same pattern, but with more overlap.
abundance: A minority of CD4 T cells and one of the larger groups in the memory CD4 T-cell pool of human blood (CXCR3-positive, CCR6-negative); exact proportions depend on how the cells are defined. They are scarce in resting lymph nodes and rise during infection.
